briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for August 11, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Phenomena Striking the World and Their Repercussions
sections.content: Today, the world faces severe threats from extreme climate phenomena such as record-breaking heatwaves, droughts, and wildfires [4, 47]. Last July, global ocean temperatures reached an all-time high, and Europe is suffering from heatwaves, droughts, and wildfires [8]. In particular, the UK Met Office predicts that the summer of 2026 will be the hottest on record for the UK, with widespread drought already declared [73, 76]. These climate changes are causing widespread damage across ecosystems, posing an existential threat to England's green spaces, endangering the survival of tree seedlings in Michigan's forests, and promoting the growth of toxic algae in water bodies [48, 52, 53, 67]. Water shortages due to drought and wildfires are causing severe water crises globally, including in Puerto Rico, Europe's Rhine and Po rivers, and the US Colorado River, with parched lands and depleted reservoirs observed everywhere [77, 78].

sections.title: ⚠️ Domestic Climate Crisis: A Test for Livelihoods and Policies
sections.content: Domestically, severe damage from extreme climate phenomena is occurring, with 7 out of 10 farms, in particular, suffering from heatwaves and heavy rains, and even facility greenhouses unable to withstand the conditions [6]. These extreme heatwaves are leaving a psychological phenomenon known as 'climate depression' among citizens, affecting society as a whole [7]. A national firefighting mobilization order was issued due to severe drought in the Gyeongnam region, deploying firefighting forces nationwide [42]. Amidst the heatwaves, construction and delivery workers are demanding legislation for work stoppages and wage preservation, and human rights issues in prisons lacking air conditioning facilities have also been raised [43, 44, 46]. Furthermore, over the past 17 months, the National Assembly's Special Committee on Climate Crisis has delayed amendments to the Carbon Neutrality Act and passed no bills [10, 41]. The issue of renewable energy output curtailment in the Honam region, accounting for half of the total curtailment due to insufficient transmission grids, also highlights the limitations of domestic climate policies and infrastructure [45].

sections.title: 🌱 Policy Shift to Accelerate Renewable Energy Deployment
sections.content: In a significant advancement for domestic renewable energy deployment, the government has decided to introduce national caps on setback distance regulations for solar and wind power generation facilities [17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 26, 27, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36, 39]. Consequently, solar power facilities can now be installed within a maximum of 200m from residential areas, and wind power facilities within a maximum of 1500m, which is expected to resolve excessive regulations that varied by local government and accelerate renewable energy deployment [25]. Jeonbuk Province is strengthening energy innovation infrastructure connectivity and promoting the advancement of its renewable energy ecosystem [31]. In Chungnam, efforts to expand renewable energy are active, with plans to construct solar power plants on public idle land and utilize up to 50% of the profits for community welfare [32, 37, 38, 40]. Naju City also demonstrated a best practice by achieving an A grade, placing it in the top 10% nationwide in the evaluation of new and renewable energy business plans [24, 35].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Spreading Local Community Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Climate Adaptation
sections.content: Voluntary and active efforts by local communities to respond to the climate crisis are expanding. Sangju City has embarked on establishing a basic plan for crop development and future agricultural strategies to respond to climate change [1, 2], and the Jeonbuk Provincial Council has announced its intention to create a stable income structure for farmers in response to the climate crisis [3]. Changes due to the climate crisis are also affecting the operation of the Geumgang Weir, with 'flexible operation' emerging as an alternative [5]. Furthermore, Gimcheon City and Jeonju City are spreading small, everyday carbon-neutral practices through citizen-participatory campaigns and business agreements [9, 11, 14]. Efforts in the education sector are also active, with Superintendent Ahn Min-seok declaring a commitment to expand carbon-neutral practices tailored to school characteristics across Gyeonggi education and initiate a major transformation in school carbon-neutral education [12, 15, 16].

sections.title: 🌍 International Solidarity and Complex Challenges in Responding to Climate Change
sections.content: The international community is responding to the complex threats of climate change in various ways. Young African Catholics are fighting climate change based on their faith [51, 58], and a poll also revealed that voters do not favor candidates who avoid climate change issues [59]. In Türkiye, the COP31 Advisory Committee held its first meeting in preparation for the UN Climate Change Summit, setting the stage for international discussions [66]. Meanwhile, ways to leverage nature's resilience are also being explored, such as research indicating that hidden fungal networks help plants survive climate change [71]. However, misinformation about climate change is hindering progress towards solutions [55], and research suggesting that AI's potential climate benefits could be overshadowed by its role in promoting fossil fuels, leading to more greenhouse gas pollution, demonstrates the dual nature of new technologies [75]. Furthermore, the criticism that fossil fuel subsidies exacerbate the climate crisis remains a significant challenge to be addressed [74].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing demonstrates that even amidst the extreme climate crisis facing the world, hope is being found through improvements in renewable energy policies and active participation from local communities. Responding to climate change requires the implementation of policies based on continuous international solidarity and scientific insight. This concludes the climate briefing for August 11, 2026.

articles.description: On June 18, Chairman Kim Jeong-ho addressed agenda items concerning the appointment of a secretary and the formation of subcommittees during the first plenary session of the Climate Crisis Special Committee in the latter half of the 22nd National Assembly. articles.original_title: 멈추면 굶고, 달리면 탈진…‘40도 폭염’ 배송 노동의 딜레마
articles.description: Despite recommendations for 'work stoppage' at 35 degrees Celsius, the absence of mandatory enforcement for employers raises questions about their effectiveness. Gig and platform workers, compensated per delivery, face the dilemma of increased workload during heatwaves while still being held responsible for delays. Transport workers are urgently calling for measures such as 'climate unemployment benefits' to ensure their right to rest. This situation is highlighted by an incident on the 4th, when a severe heatwave warning was issued for the Seoul metropolitan area, where a delivery rider in their 50s collapsed on a road in Yangju, Gyeonggi Province, exhibiting symptoms of heat exhaustion.

summary.phenomenon: Delivery workers are facing significant health threats due to extreme heat, exemplified by an incident on the 4th when a severe heatwave warning was issued for the Seoul metropolitan area, and a delivery rider in their 50s collapsed from heat exhaustion in Yangju, Gyeonggi Province.
summary.cause: The issue stems from a structural problem where recommendations for work stoppages at 35 degrees Celsius lack mandatory employer enforcement, diminishing their effectiveness. Additionally, gig and platform workers, compensated on a per-delivery basis, are compelled to continue or even increase their work during heatwaves.
summary.outlook: Transport workers are urgently advocating for the implementation of systems, such as climate unemployment benefits, to ensure their right to rest during extreme weather conditions.
